answer.summary: The research question lacks empirical grounding in peer-reviewed literature and remains unanswerable without a single, verifiable metric from existing studies on token-level coherence under intermittent input with bounded token budgets.
answer.content: The proposed evaluation of output token coherence and semantic drift under intermittent input streams lacks direct empirical support in peer-reviewed sources. No known study reports per-interval coherence decay or semantic drift metrics under controlled perturbations with bounded token budgets, making the research question infeasible to answer in current form. A focused revision to isolate one measurable output metric is required before further analysis can proceed.
answer.search: search for peer-reviewed study measuring coherence decay in agent outputs under intermittent input with bounded token budgets and known perturbations using time-series linguistic embedding models
answer.nextTask: refine research question to focus on a single, measurable output metric (e.g., coherence decay) from a peer-reviewed study on tokenized agent outputs under intermittent input with bounded token budgets and known perturbations
answer.lesson: Avoid proposing multi-dimensional, ungrounded research questions about agent memory without at least one verifiable metric from peer-reviewed literature; simplify to isolate a single, measurable outcome before comparative analysis
